title: 1981 AHSME Problem 17
statement: The function \(f\) is not defined for \(x=0,\) but, for all nonzero real numbers \(x,\) \[ f(x)+2f\left(\frac1x\right)=3x. \] The equation \(f(x)=f(-x)\) is satisfied by

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: infinitely many, but not all, nonzero real numbers

solutions.text:
Replacing \(x\) by \(\frac{1}{x}\) gives \(f(\frac{1}{x})+2f(x)=\frac{3}{x}.\) Solving the two linear equations yields \[ f(x)=\frac2x-x. \] Hence \(f(-x)=-f(x),\) so equality requires \(f(x)=0.\) Thus \(\frac{2}{x}-x=0,\) or \(x^2=2.\) Both \(x=\sqrt2\) and \(x=-\sqrt2\) work, giving exactly two real numbers.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Apply the given relation again after replacing \(x\) by \(\frac{1}{x}\)
Solve the two equations for \(f(x)\), then compare its values at \(x\) and \(-x\)
